title: Verify memory-unit mismatch in Central backend worker selection
problem: Startup obtains memory limits in bytes but determines worker count using a 1100000 threshold. The original function returns four workers even for 512 MiB or 1 GiB inputs.
humanitarian_relevance: Resource-appropriate server operation could support constrained humanitarian field-data deployments. Specific adoption, resource savings and avoided outages are unmeasured.

evidence.claim: The startup file is byte-identical on inspected master and next revisions; eight original-function probe cases pass, including threshold boundaries and zero/high-memory controls.
A contributor reports production logs showing four workers at 2023899136 bytes; this high-memory example does not alone distinguish the threshold interpretations.

GitHub returned the exact prepared scope inquiry by humanifest-bot at 2026-09-09T03:51:43Z. The issue remained open/unassigned and next matched the audited SHA immediately before posting. No maintainer approval is established.

code_surface: files/service/scripts/start-odk.sh: get_memory_limit and determine_worker_count; test/check-scripts.sh and test/service/service.spec.js.
proposed_change: Confirm the intended threshold units and strict boundary, then normalize units and add focused tests on a bot fork targeting next. Keep #2170 broader sizing policy separate; no implementation prepared.
tests: Eight hash-checked pure-function Bash cases pass. No cgroup discovery, Docker startup, target suite or resource benchmark executed.
environment: Read-only source downloads plus isolated function execution with only synthetic positional arguments. No target clone or install. Full startup reads secrets, writes configuration, migrates a database and starts services; do not source it for tests.
maintainer: Scoped inquiry delivered as humanifest-bot at 2026-09-09T03:51:43Z; asks whether byte normalization and boundary tests are wanted separately from #2170, and requests intended threshold and AI contribution requirements. Delivery is not scope confirmation; no target implementation prepared.
risks: Startup behavior is operationally consequential. Preserve unknown-memory fallback and obtain agreement on threshold/worker policy. Do not claim measured compute savings from worker-count arithmetic.
